questions.prompt: A different lab runs your published code on your published data and gets your numbers. Which term fits best?
questions.explanation: Different team, same artifacts: reproducibility. Replicability needs new data/setup.

questions.prompt: Per-run SD is 4 points and you report the mean of 8 seeds. Standard error of your reported mean? (3 decimals)
Per-run SD is 4 points and you report the mean of 8 seeds. What is the 95% tolerance for the difference between two independent re-runs, 1.96*sqrt(2)*sigma/sqrt(n)? (2 decimals)
Why sort keys before hashing a configuration dictionary?
options: To remove duplicate keys that would otherwise appear in the configuration.
To make the hash shorter, since the sorted keys compress better in storage.
Equal configurations then give the same digest regardless of the key order.
To encrypt the configuration so that it cannot be read back from the digest.
questions.explanation: Canonical serialisation makes the hash a function of content only.

questions.prompt: After verification, the manifest reports that raw_data.csv has a different hash than recorded. What is the correct action?
options: Delete the manifest and rebuild it later from the files that are currently present.
Ignore it if the figure looks the same, since the visible result is unchanged anyway.
Update the manifest silently to match the file, so the verification passes again.
Stop, find what changed and why, then restore it or record a new versioned run first.
questions.explanation: A changed input invalidates the chain of evidence until explained.

questions.prompt: In IEEE double precision, what does (1e16 + 1.0) - 1e16 evaluate to?
questions.explanation: 1e16+1.0 rounds back to 1e16, so the result is 0.0.

questions.prompt: A collaborator cannot reproduce your Figure 2. List the artifacts you should have shared and the checks you would run, in order.
rubric: Raw data, code at a commit hash, environment lock, configuration and seeds.
A manifest of hashes verified first, then a clean-room re-run.
A stated tolerance derived from seed variance for numeric agreement.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
